The term neuroleptic is sometimes used to describe those antipsychotics that have effects on the extrapyrami- dal system The difference in action between anxiolytics and hyp- notics is mainly one of degree and the same drug or group of drugs can have both effects, larger doses be- ing necessary to produce a state of sleep. The benzodiazepines (typified by Diazepam, p.986) replaced the barbiturates (typified by Amobarbital, p.961) and related sedatives as the major group of drugs used as anxiolytics and hypnotics. Some benzo- diazepines are also used for their muscle relaxant and anticonvulsant properties. Newer anxiolytics include buspirone (p.965), a drug that affects serotonin neuro- transmission. The classical antipsychotics (typified by Chlorpro- mazine, p.969) include the butyrophenones, the diphe- nylbutylpiperidines, the indole derivatives, the pheno- thiazines, and the thioxanthenes.
